name: Goa
summary: Sun-soaked beaches, Portuguese lanes and sunsets that turn into beach parties.

name: Manali
summary: Pine forests, snow peaks and café-hopping in Old Manali.

name: Jaipur
summary: The Pink City: palaces, forts and bazaars bursting with colour.

name: Kerala Backwaters
summary: Drift through palm-lined backwaters on a houseboat in God’s Own Country.

name: Ladakh
summary: High-altitude deserts, turquoise lakes and monasteries on the roof of the world.

name: Varanasi
summary: The world’s oldest living city — ghats, ganga aarti and legendary street food.

name: Rishikesh
summary: Yoga capital on the Ganga: suspension bridges, evening aarti and white-water rafting.

image.credit: McKay Savage from London, UK · CC BY 2.0

name: Dharamshala & McLeod Ganj
summary: Little Lhasa under the Dhauladhars: monasteries, Tibetan momos and the Triund trek.

name: Shimla
summary: The old summer capital: Mall Road, colonial churches and the toy train through the hills.

name: Spiti Valley
summary: A cold desert at 3,800 m: cliff-top monasteries, fossil villages and endless night skies.

image.credit: Original: Kulbhushan Singh Suryawanshi ( website ) Derivati… · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Darjeeling
summary: Tea gardens, the toy train and Kanchenjunga at sunrise from Tiger Hill.

name: Gangtok
summary: Sikkim’s tidy hill capital: monasteries, MG Marg and high lakes towards Nathu La.

name: Pelling
summary: Kanchenjunga at arm’s length, Pemayangtse Monastery and the ruins of Rabdentse, Sikkim’s old capital.

name: Lachung & Yumthang
summary: A North Sikkim village under snow peaks, and the rhododendron valley of Yumthang above it.

name: Ravangla
summary: Buddha Park’s giant statue, Ralang Monastery and the Temi tea garden on a quiet Sikkim ridge.

name: Kalimpong
summary: Orchid nurseries, hilltop monasteries and views over the Teesta to Kanchenjunga.

name: Srinagar
summary: Shikaras on Dal Lake, Mughal gardens and houseboats under the Zabarwan hills.

name: Gulmarg
summary: A meadow of flowers in summer and India’s best ski slopes in winter, with a gondola up Apharwat.

name: Pahalgam
summary: The Lidder valley’s pine meadows — Betaab, Aru and Baisaran — and the start of the Amarnath Yatra.

name: Sonamarg
summary: The meadow of gold: Thajiwas glacier, trout streams and the road up to Zoji La.

image.credit: Gktambe at English Wikipedia · Public domain

name: Katra & Vaishno Devi
summary: Base of the 12 km climb to the Vaishno Devi cave shrine in the Trikuta hills.

name: Kasol & Parvati Valley
summary: The pine-lined Parvati river, Manikaran’s hot springs and the trek up to Kheerganga.

image.credit: Zoeacs at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Dalhousie & Khajjiar
summary: Colonial churches on five hills, and Khajjiar’s meadow ringed by deodar forest.

name: Bir Billing
summary: India’s paragliding capital: take off at Billing, land among Tibetan monasteries in Bir.

image.credit: Gagansalaria at English Wikipedia · Public domain

name: Kasauli
summary: A quiet cantonment of pine walks, Christ Church and sunset over the plains.

name: Kinnaur (Kalpa & Sangla)
summary: Apple orchards under Kinner Kailash, Kalpa’s views and Chitkul, the last village on the road to Tibet.

name: Palampur
summary: Tea gardens of Kangra under the snowy Dhauladhar range, with old temples close by.

name: Mussoorie
summary: The Queen of the Hills: Mall Road, Kempty Falls and Landour’s quiet lanes above the Doon.

name: Nainital
summary: Boats on Naini Lake, Snow View point and the lake country of Kumaon around it.

name: Auli
summary: Ski slopes and oak meadows facing Nanda Devi, with a long gondola up from Joshimath.

name: Kedarnath
summary: The jyotirlinga temple at 3,583 m beneath snow peaks, reached by a trek from Gaurikund.

name: Valley of Flowers & Hemkund
summary: A UNESCO alpine valley in bloom each monsoon, and the glacial lake of Hemkund Sahib above Ghangaria.
highlights: Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks

name: Jim Corbett National Park
summary: India’s oldest national park: tiger safaris through the sal forests and grasslands of Dhikala.

name: Chopta & Tungnath
summary: Alpine meadows and the trek to Tungnath, the highest Shiva temple, with Chandrashila above.

image.credit: Senthilnath G T, XS · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Munsiyari
summary: Face to face with the five Panchachuli peaks, and the gateway to the Milam glacier trek.

image.credit: Capnraib at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Kausani
summary: A 300 km sweep of Himalayan peaks at sunrise, tea estates and Gandhi’s Anasakti Ashram.

name: Almora & Binsar
summary: An old Kumaoni hill town of temples and bal mithai, with the oak forests of Binsar above.

name: Nubra Valley
summary: Over Khardung La to sand dunes, double-humped camels and Diskit’s giant Maitreya Buddha.

name: Jaisalmer
summary: The Golden City: a living sandstone fort, carved havelis and nights on the Thar dunes.

name: Jodhpur
summary: The Blue City under Mehrangarh Fort, with spice markets and stepwells in the old town.

name: Udaipur
summary: The City of Lakes: palaces on Lake Pichola, rooftop sunsets and old-city lanes.

name: Pushkar
summary: A holy lake ringed by 52 ghats, the rare Brahma temple and the famous camel fair.

name: Bikaner
summary: Junagarh Fort, the camel research farm and the original home of bhujia.

image.credit: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra from Paris, France · CC BY 2.0

name: Agra
summary: The Taj Mahal at dawn, Agra Fort and Mughal tombs along the Yamuna.

image.credit: Taj_Mahal,_Agra,_India_edit2.jpg : Yann ; edited by King of… · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Delhi
summary: Seven cities in one: Old Delhi’s food lanes, Mughal tombs and Lutyens’ boulevards.

name: Amritsar
summary: The Golden Temple’s langar, Jallianwala Bagh and kulchas worth the trip alone.

image.credit: This picture has been taken by Oleg Yunakov · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Bodh Gaya
summary: Where the Buddha found enlightenment: the Mahabodhi Temple and monasteries of many nations.

name: Lucknow
summary: Nawabi city of kebabs and chikan embroidery, with the Bara Imambara’s maze.

name: Hampi
summary: The ruined Vijayanagara capital among giant boulders, with sunrise from Matanga Hill.

name: Hyderabad
summary: Charminar, Golconda Fort and the biryani the city is famous for.

name: Ellora & Aurangabad
summary: The rock-cut Kailasa temple, Buddhist and Jain caves, and Daulatabad’s hill fort.

name: Mysuru
summary: The illuminated Mysore Palace, Chamundi Hill and silk, sandalwood and Mysore pak.

name: Badami, Aihole & Pattadakal
summary: Chalukya cave temples above a red-sandstone lake, and the cradle of temple architecture.

name: Vijayapura (Bijapur)
summary: The Gol Gumbaz whispering gallery and the Adil Shahi tombs and mosques.

name: Munnar
summary: Tea estates rolling over the hills, misty viewpoints and the Nilgiri tahr of Eravikulam.

name: Coorg
summary: Coffee estates, waterfalls and Kodava pork curry in the misty hills of Kodagu.

name: Ooty
summary: The Nilgiri toy train, botanical gardens and tea country around the lake.

name: Wayanad
summary: Rainforest, the Edakkal caves’ ancient carvings and wildlife at Muthanga.

name: Kodaikanal
summary: A star-shaped lake, pine forests and cliff-edge views over the plains.

name: Mahabaleshwar
summary: Strawberry farms, Sahyadri viewpoints and Shivaji’s Pratapgad fort nearby.

name: Chikkamagaluru
summary: Where Indian coffee began: estates under Mullayanagiri, Karnataka’s highest peak, and Baba Budangiri.

name: Coonoor
summary: Tea estates, Sim’s Park and Dolphin’s Nose — a quieter stop on the Nilgiri toy train.

name: Thekkady (Periyar)
summary: Boat safaris on Periyar Lake among wild elephants, and spice gardens in Kumily.

name: Kochi
summary: Chinese fishing nets, Jew Town’s spice lanes and Kathakali in Fort Kochi.

name: Mumbai
summary: Gateway of India, Marine Drive at night and vada pav on every corner.

name: Gokarna
summary: A temple town with quiet coves — Om, Kudle and Half Moon beaches on a cliff trail.

name: Varkala
summary: Red laterite cliffs above the Arabian Sea, with cafés on the edge and a 2,000-year-old temple.

name: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock)
summary: Radhanagar Beach, clear-water snorkelling and dives over coral reefs.

name: Shillong
summary: The Scotland of the East: pine hills, Ward’s Lake, live music and waterfalls nearby.

name: Cherrapunji (Sohra)
summary: Living root bridges, plunging waterfalls and caves in one of the wettest places on earth.

name: Tawang
summary: India’s largest monastery at 3,000 m, high lakes and the drive over Sela Pass.

name: Kaziranga
summary: Home of two-thirds of the world’s one-horned rhinos; jeep and elephant-grass safaris.

name: Kohima
summary: Naga hill capital: the WWII cemetery, Dzukou Valley and the Hornbill Festival in December.
highlights: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral, Kohima

name: Majuli
summary: A huge river island on the Brahmaputra with Vaishnavite satras and mask-making.

name: Ziro
summary: Apatani villages and rice fields in a pine valley, home of the Ziro music festival.

name: Mawlynnong
summary: A famously clean Khasi village, the living root bridge at Riwai and views over the Bangladesh plains.

image.credit: Arghya Banik from Bangladesh · CC BY 2.0

name: Bomdila
summary: Monasteries and apple orchards with Himalayan views, on the way up to Sela Pass.

name: Mechuka
summary: A remote valley on the Siyom river near the China border, with an old monastery and snow peaks all round.

image.credit: Quentin Talon & Mario Geiger · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Namdapha National Park
summary: Rainforest rising to snow peaks: home of four big cats and the hoolock gibbon.

name: Guwahati
summary: Gateway to the North-East: Kamakhya Temple, Brahmaputra cruises and Umananda island.

name: Manas National Park
summary: A UNESCO tiger reserve on the Bhutan border: golden langurs, wild buffalo and river forest.

image.credit: Pankaj from Bangalore, India · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Sivasagar
summary: The old Ahom capital: Rang Ghar, Talatal Ghar and temples beside a great tank.

name: Haflong
summary: Assam’s only hill station: a lake, the blue hills of Dima Hasao and the Jatinga ridge.

name: Tezpur & Nameri
summary: Ancient ruins and Agnigarh hill by the Brahmaputra, with river rafting at Nameri nearby.

name: Imphal & Loktak Lake
summary: Kangla Fort, the women-run Ima Market and the floating islands of Loktak Lake.

name: Aizawl
summary: A ridge-top city of churches and Mizo crafts, with the Reiek viewpoint close by.

name: Agartala
summary: The white Ujjayanta Palace, the lake palace of Neermahal and Tripura’s old temples.

name: Unakoti
summary: Huge rock-cut Shiva faces and a hillside of ancient reliefs in the Tripura forest.

name: Bali
summary: Rice terraces, temple gates and surf breaks with sunset beach clubs.

name: Paris
summary: Cafés, galleries and golden-hour walks along the Seine.

name: Tokyo
summary: Neon nights, quiet shrines and the best food crawl of your life.

name: Santorini
summary: Whitewashed cliffs, blue domes and the most famous sunset in Europe.

name: Dubai
summary: Sky-high towers, desert dunes and malls with their own ski slopes.

name: Interlaken
summary: Alpine lakes, paragliding and train rides straight out of a postcard.
